title.en: Let a declared bond list define connectivity

summary: Take connectivity from the structure data, and if bonds are inferred from distances, state the cutoff and show it as inference.
objective: Keep chemical connectivity a modelled fact rather than a by-product of a rendering heuristic.
applies_when: A molecular or lattice structure is loaded from a file or generated.
Bonds are drawn between atoms, or hydrogen bonds and contacts are shown.
The user can move atoms or change the structure interactively.
example_prompts: Show the water network with hydrogen bonds marked as interactions, not covalent bonds.
Load the structure and draw its bonds from the file.
negative_signals: Purely visual molecule-like graphics with no chemical claim.
Coarse-grained or abstract models where bonds are not represented at all.
not_for: Purely visual molecule-like graphics with no chemical claim.
Coarse-grained or abstract models where bonds are not represented at all.

principles: Connectivity is part of the structure, not part of the drawing. When bonds are recomputed from positions every frame, moving an atom silently rewrites the chemistry.
A distance threshold is an inference procedure with parameters. Used without disclosure it produces bonds that appear and vanish as geometry changes, which viewers read as chemical events.
Different interaction types deserve different visual treatment and different rules: covalent bonds, hydrogen bonds and contacts are not interchangeable lines.
If the scene lets the user move atoms, it must say whether the bond graph is fixed, recomputed, or edited by the user.
implementation: Read connectivity from the source structure where one exists and keep it as data attached to the atoms.
If bonds must be inferred, state the rule and the cutoff on the artifact and mark inferred bonds distinctly from declared ones.
Give non-covalent interactions their own representation and their own criteria, and label them in the legend.
Decide the editing model explicitly: rigid graph with movable geometry, or a structure editor where bonds can change and the change is an action.
Preserve atom identity across edits so the graph and any per-atom annotation stay attached.
observable_checks: Move an atom to the edge of the threshold and watch for bonds flickering; that is the inference showing through.
Compare the drawn bond count against the connectivity in the source data.
Confirm hydrogen bonds and contacts are visually and semantically distinct from covalent bonds.
Undo an edit and confirm the graph returns exactly, not approximately.

creative_affordances: Stylised bond rendering, from tubes to dashed fields to animated interactions, is free once the underlying graph is authoritative.
A deliberate distance-based contact map is a legitimate analysis view when presented as one.
known_limits: Authored data-model guidance; no chemistry is asserted and no structure file has been validated for this record.
It does not recommend any specific bond-perception algorithm or cutoff value.
